# Cardano Client Lib — complete documentation

Latest preview 0.8.0-pre7 (Java 17+) · Latest stable 0.7.3 (Java 11+) · Conway era · generated 2026-11-02
Source: https://cardano-client.dev

---

# Using Cardano Client Lib with AI

Source: https://cardano-client.dev/ai/
Summary: Machine-readable artifacts, agent rules, and the fastest way to get an AI coding agent writing correct CCL code.

Coding agents write a lot of Cardano off-chain Java now. This site publishes the artifacts an
agent needs so it generates code against the **current** API rather than a stale snapshot from its
training data.

## Point your agent here first

| Artifact | URL | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| Curated index | [`/llms.txt`](/llms.txt) | Every page, grouped, with the "which API do I use" table at the top. Follows the [llmstxt.org](https://llmstxt.org) convention. |
| Full corpus | [`/llms-full.txt`](/llms-full.txt) | The entire documentation site as one plain-text file, for bulk ingestion. |
| Starter pack | [`/ai/starter-pack/`](/ai/starter-pack/) · [raw](/ai/starter-pack.md) | The rules that keep an agent from making the common mistakes. **Read this before generating code.** |
| Module catalog | [`/ai/catalog.json`](/ai/catalog.json) | Machine-readable: every published module, its artifact id, its canonical entry-point class, and its recommendation tier. Generated from `settings.gradle` and `gradle.properties`, so it cannot drift from the build. |

The catalog and both `.txt` files are regenerated on every build. If the library gains a module,
these artifacts describe it the same day.

## Why this exists

Asked to "send 5 ADA on preview with cardano-client-lib", agents reliably produce code that
compiles and is wrong. The recurring failures are specific:

- Pairing `Networks.preview()` with `Constants.BLOCKFROST_MAINNET_URL` — the network and the
  backend URL are configured separately, and nothing stops you mismatching them.
- Calling `complete()` and then reporting success, when `complete()` only submits. It does not
  wait for the transaction to be included in a block.
- Reaching for the `function` module's `TxBuilder` composition primitives instead of QuickTx.
  It works, but it is the low-level layer and mistakes there are silent.
- Generating `WatchableQuickTxBuilder`, a class that **has never existed in a released version**.
  TxFlow is the multi-step API.
- Emitting Babbage-era patterns for Conway-only operations (DRep registration, votes, treasury
  withdrawals).

The starter pack addresses each of these directly.

## Rules files for specific tools

Drop the starter pack into whichever file your tool reads, so the rules load automatically
instead of relying on the agent to fetch a URL:

```bash
# Claude Code
curl -o CLAUDE.md https://cardano-client.dev/ai/starter-pack.md

# Cursor
mkdir -p .cursor/rules && \
  curl -o .cursor/rules/cardano-client-lib.mdc https://cardano-client.dev/ai/starter-pack.md

# GitHub Copilot
mkdir -p .github && \
  curl -o .github/copilot-instructions.md https://cardano-client.dev/ai/starter-pack.md
```

For an agent that can fetch URLs at run time, pointing it at `/llms.txt` is enough — the index
links onward to everything else.

## Verifying what an agent produces

Generated transaction code should be run before you trust it. The cheapest loop is
[Yaci DevKit](https://devkit.yaci.xyz/#get-started), a local Cardano devnet with pre-funded
accounts and instant blocks — no faucet, no API key, no waiting on a public testnet.

Point the backend at `http://localhost:8080/api/v1/` and the same code you would run on preview
works locally, so an agent can execute what it wrote and read a real transaction hash back.

- [AI Starter Pack](/ai/starter-pack/) — the rules themselves
- [Key APIs at a glance](/start-here/key-apis/) — a quick tour of the main APIs
- [Modules & artifacts](/reference/modules/) — full dependency reference

# AI Starter Pack

Source: https://cardano-client.dev/ai/starter-pack/
Summary: Everything an AI agent needs to write correct cardano-client-lib code on the first try. Ingest this before generating any CCL code.

> **Read this whole document before generating cardano-client-lib code.** It is optimized for
> machine ingestion, not for learning. Humans should start at
> [Your first transaction](/learn/simple-transfer/) instead.

Target version: the [latest preview](/start-here/installation/#versions) · Ledger era: **Conway** · Java **17+** · Group `com.bloxbean.cardano`

---

## 1. Choose the API before writing a line

| Task | Use | Module |
|---|---|---|
| One transaction — send, mint, delegate, register, vote, call a script | `QuickTxBuilder` + `Tx` | `cardano-client-quicktx` |
| A plan expressed as configuration rather than code | `TxPlan` (YAML/JSON) | `cardano-client-quicktx` |
| Several dependent transactions, in order, with rollback handling | `FlowEngine` | `cardano-client-txflow` |
| Continuous submission with exactly-once and durable restart | `TxFlowStream` | `cardano-client-txflow` |
| A proof an Aiken validator can verify on-chain | `MpfTrie` | `cardano-client-merkle-patricia-forestry` |

**QuickTx is the default.** Only move up this table when the task genuinely needs the extra
machinery.

### Never generate these

| Do not use | Why | Use instead |
|---|---|---|
| `WatchableQuickTxBuilder` | **Does not exist.** Never shipped in any release. If your training data suggests it, that memory is wrong. | `FlowEngine` (TxFlow) |
| `com.bloxbean.cardano.client.function.*` (`TxBuilder`, `TxOutputBuilder`, `InputBuilders`, `BalanceTxBuilders`) | The internal implementation layer beneath QuickTx. It works, but mistakes are silent and it is far more verbose. | `QuickTx` |
| `ScriptTx`, on 0.8.0 previews | **Deprecated in the 0.8.0 previews**, where every operation is also on `Tx`. Not deprecated in stable 0.7.x, where it is the right API for scripts. | `Tx` on previews |
| `FlowExecutor` | Compatibility API. Combines definition and execution concerns; not the canonical durable path. | `FlowEngine` |
| `JellyfishMerkleTree` for on-chain proofs | Not Aiken-compatible. Off-chain authenticated state only. | `MpfTrie` |

---

## 2. The five mistakes agents actually make

### 2.1 Mismatching the network and the backend URL

The `Network` (used for address derivation) and the backend URL (used for queries) are configured
**separately**. Nothing validates that they agree, so a mismatch produces addresses on one network
and queries against another.

```java
// WRONG — preview addresses, mainnet backend. Compiles, fails at run time.
Account account = Account.createFromMnemonic(Networks.preview(), mnemonic);
BackendService backend = new BFBackendService(Constants.BLOCKFROST_MAINNET_URL, projectId);

// RIGHT — both preview.
Account account = Account.createFromMnemonic(Networks.preview(), mnemonic);
BackendService backend = new BFBackendService(Constants.BLOCKFROST_PREVIEW_URL, projectId);
```

Matched pairs — `Constants` here is
`com.bloxbean.cardano.client.backend.blockfrost.common.Constants`:

| Network | `Networks` factory | Blockfrost URL constant |
|---|---|---|
| Mainnet | `Networks.mainnet()` | `BLOCKFROST_MAINNET_URL` |
| Preprod | `Networks.preprod()` | `BLOCKFROST_PREPROD_URL` |
| Preview | `Networks.preview()` | `BLOCKFROST_PREVIEW_URL` |
| Local devnet (Yaci DevKit) | `Networks.testnet()` | `http://localhost:8080/api/v1/` |

All test networks use network id 0, so `Networks.testnet()`, `Networks.preview()` and `Networks.preprod()` give the same addresses. Use the constant that names your network when you know it.

### 2.2 Treating `complete()` as confirmation

```java
TxResult result = quickTxBuilder.compose(tx)
        .withSigner(SignerProviders.signerFrom(account))
        .complete();          // submits ONLY — does not wait
```

`complete()` returns as soon as the node accepts the transaction for propagation. The transaction
may still fail to be included, or be rolled back.

| Method | Returns | Waits for a block? |
|---|---|---|
| `complete()` | `TxResult` | No |
| `completeAndWait()` | `TxResult` | Yes |
| `completeAndWaitAsync()` | `CompletableFuture<TxResult>` | Yes, off-thread |

Use `completeAndWait()` unless you have a specific reason not to, and check the status:

```java
TxResult result = quickTxBuilder.compose(tx)
        .withSigner(SignerProviders.signerFrom(account))
        .completeAndWait();

if (result.getTxStatus() == TxStatus.CONFIRMED) {
    System.out.println("Confirmed: " + result.getTxHash());
} else {
    System.err.println("Not confirmed: " + result.getTxStatus());
}
```

`TxStatus` values: `SUBMITTED`, `PENDING`, `CONFIRMED`, `FAILED`, `TIMEOUT`.

:::note[`TxResult` extends `Result<String>`]
Assigning to `Result<String>` still compiles — you will see that in older examples — but it
discards `getTxStatus()`, which is the only way to tell a submitted transaction from a confirmed
one. Declare the variable as `TxResult`. `isSuccessful()` and `getResponse()` are inherited from
`Result` and remain available.
:::

### 2.3 Reaching for the `function` module

If you find yourself writing `TxBuilder`, `TxOutputBuilder`, `InputBuilders.createFromSender(...)`
or `BalanceTxBuilders.balanceTx(...)`, stop. QuickTx expresses the same thing in a few lines:

```java
// The whole of a payment, including balancing and fee calculation.
Tx tx = new Tx()
        .payToAddress(receiverAddress, Amount.ada(10))
        .from(senderAddress);
```

The `function` module is documented under
[Composable functions](/reference/composable-functions/) for the rare cases QuickTx cannot cover.
Do not generate it by default.

### 2.4 Assuming pre-Conway APIs

This library targets the **Conway** era. Governance is first-class on `Tx`:

```java
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.governance.GovId;

// A bech32 DRep id (CIP-105) becomes a DRep via GovId.toDrep.
DRep drep = GovId.toDrep(account.drepId());

Tx tx = new Tx()
        .registerDRep(account, anchor)                  // DRep registration
        .delegateVotingPowerTo(stakeAddress, drep)      // vote delegation
        .createVote(voter, govActionId, Vote.YES)       // voting
        .createProposal(govAction, rewardAccount, anchor)
        .from(senderAddress);
```

`delegateVotingPowerTo` takes a `DRep`, not a bech32 id string — convert with `GovId.toDrep(...)`.

If your training data has no `registerDRep` / `createVote` / `delegateVotingPowerTo` on `Tx`, it
predates Conway support. See [Governance API](/governance/overview/).

### 2.5 Ignoring the datum-hash filter in coin selection

The default UTXO selection strategy **skips UTXOs carrying a datum hash**. That is usually right
for ordinary payments and wrong when you mean to spend a script output. When collecting from a
script address, pass the UTXOs explicitly with `collectFrom(...)` rather than relying on
selection.

---

## 3. Canonical patterns

### 3.1 Send ADA

```java
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.account.Account;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.api.model.Amount;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.backend.api.BackendService;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.backend.blockfrost.common.Constants;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.backend.blockfrost.service.BFBackendService;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.common.model.Networks;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.function.helper.SignerProviders;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.quicktx.QuickTxBuilder;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.quicktx.Tx;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.quicktx.TxResult;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.quicktx.TxStatus;

Account sender = Account.createFromMnemonic(Networks.preview(), senderMnemonic);
BackendService backend =
        new BFBackendService(Constants.BLOCKFROST_PREVIEW_URL, projectId);

Tx tx = new Tx()
        .payToAddress(receiverAddress, Amount.ada(10))
        .from(sender.baseAddress());

TxResult result = new QuickTxBuilder(backend)
        .compose(tx)
        .withSigner(SignerProviders.signerFrom(sender))
        .completeAndWait();
```

`SignerProviders` lives in the `function` package but is the correct, canonical way to sign a
QuickTx transaction — it is the one part of that package you should generate.

### 3.2 Mint a native token

```java
Policy policy = PolicyUtil.createMultiSigScriptAllPolicy("my-policy", 1);
Asset asset = new Asset("MyToken", BigInteger.valueOf(1000));

Tx tx = new Tx()
        .mintAssets(policy.getPolicyScript(), asset, receiverAddress)
        .from(sender.baseAddress());

TxResult result = new QuickTxBuilder(backend)
        .compose(tx)
        .withSigner(SignerProviders.signerFrom(sender))
        .withSigner(SignerProviders.signerFrom(policy))   // policy key must sign too
        .completeAndWait();
```

Minting needs **two** signers: the funding account and the policy key.

### 3.3 Call a Plutus script

On the 0.8.0 previews, use `Tx` rather than `ScriptTx`. On stable 0.7.x, use `ScriptTx` with `.feePayer(...)`:

```java
Tx tx = new Tx()
        .collectFrom(scriptUtxo, redeemer)
        .attachSpendingValidator(plutusScript)
        .payToAddress(receiverAddress, Amount.ada(5))
        .from(sender.baseAddress());

TxResult result = new QuickTxBuilder(backend)
        .compose(tx)
        .withSigner(SignerProviders.signerFrom(sender))
        .completeAndWait();
```

:::caution[`ScriptTx` is deprecated in the 0.8.0 previews only]
In the previews, every `ScriptTx` operation is also on `Tx` — script inputs, validator attachment, Plutus
minting, script-protected certificates and governance. `ScriptTx` still works there. In stable 0.7.x it
isn't deprecated, and `Tx` has none of these script operations, so check which version the project uses.

To migrate, replace `new ScriptTx()` with `new Tx()`. Because `Tx` has `.from(...)`, the
separate `.feePayer(...)` step that `ScriptTx` required is no longer needed for the common case.
`Tx` has no `collectFrom(Utxo)`, and `Tx.collectFrom(List<Utxo>)` adds regular inputs, so always pass a
redeemer when spending from a script. See [Unified Tx API](/quicktx/unified-tx/).
:::

One naming trap: **native-script** minting is `mintAssets` (plural), **Plutus** minting is
`mintAsset` (singular).

### 3.4 Stake delegation

```java
Tx tx = new Tx()
        .registerStakeAddress(sender.stakeAddress())
        .delegateTo(sender.stakeAddress(), poolId)
        .from(sender.baseAddress());

TxResult result = new QuickTxBuilder(backend)
        .compose(tx)
        .withSigner(SignerProviders.signerFrom(sender))
        .withSigner(SignerProviders.stakeKeySignerFrom(sender))   // stake key signs
        .completeAndWait();
```

Delegation, deregistration and withdrawal need the **stake key** signature in addition to the payment key. Registration alone doesn't. A withdrawal also needs the stake address to have delegated its vote, for example `.delegateVotingPowerTo(address, DRep.abstain())`.

---

## 4. Signing reference

| Signer | Use for |
|---|---|
| `SignerProviders.signerFrom(account)` | Payment key. Almost every transaction. |
| `SignerProviders.signerFrom(policy)` | Native-script policy key, when minting or burning. |
| `SignerProviders.stakeKeySignerFrom(account)` | Delegation, vote delegation, deregistration, withdrawal. |
| `SignerProviders.drepKeySignerFrom(account)` | Conway DRep operations. |
| `SignerProviders.committeeHotKeySignerFrom(account)` | Conway committee hot-key votes. |
| `SignerProviders.committeeColdKeySignerFrom(account)` | Conway committee cold-key operations. |

Chain `.withSigner(...)` once per required key.

---

## 5. Dependencies

Use one version for every CCL module.

```gradle
def cclVersion = '<version>' // the latest preview, see /start-here/installation/#versions

dependencies {
    implementation "com.bloxbean.cardano:cardano-client-lib:${cclVersion}"
    implementation "com.bloxbean.cardano:cardano-client-backend-blockfrost:${cclVersion}"

    // Only if the task needs them:
    implementation "com.bloxbean.cardano:cardano-client-txflow:${cclVersion}"
    implementation "com.bloxbean.cardano:cardano-client-merkle-patricia-forestry:${cclVersion}"
}
```

`cardano-client-lib` is the aggregate that pulls in the common modules. Add a backend module —
without one there is no way to read UTXOs or submit.

The full generated list of modules, artifact ids and entry points is at
[`/ai/catalog.json`](/ai/catalog.json).

---

## 6. Verified data structures: which one

Answer in this order.

1. **Must an on-chain Aiken validator verify the proof?**
   Yes → `MpfTrie`. No → `JellyfishMerkleTree` also works, for off-chain state only.
2. **Which storage backend?**
   `merkle-patricia-forestry-rocksdb` for embedded single-process.
   `merkle-patricia-forestry-rdbms` for shared multi-process (PostgreSQL, H2, SQLite).

See [Verified structures](/verified-structures/overview/).

---

## 7. Testing generated code

Do not hand back transaction code you have not run. [Yaci DevKit](https://devkit.yaci.xyz/#get-started)
gives a local devnet with pre-funded accounts and one-second blocks. `devkitMnemonic` is the [default devnet mnemonic](/learn/test-with-yaci-devkit/#fund-an-account):

```java
BackendService backend = new BFBackendService("http://localhost:8080/api/v1/", "dummy-key");
Account sender = Account.createFromMnemonic(Networks.testnet(), devkitMnemonic);
```

No API key, no faucet, no testnet wait. If the code produces a confirmed transaction hash there,
the same code works against preview with the URL and network swapped.

# Governance API

Source: https://cardano-client.dev/governance/overview/
Summary: APIs for Cardano governance operations (DRep, Voting, Proposals)

The Governance API provides comprehensive functionality for participating in Cardano's on-chain governance system. It supports DRep registration and management, governance proposal creation, voting, and delegation operations through the QuickTx framework.

## Key Features

- **DRep Management**: Register, update, and deregister as a Delegated Representative
- **Proposal Creation**: Create various types of governance proposals (Info, Constitution, Parameter Changes, etc.)
- **Voting System**: Vote on governance proposals with different voter types
- **Delegation**: Delegate voting power to DReps
- **Anchor Support**: Attach metadata anchors to proposals and votes
- **Multi-Signature Support**: Support for committee and stake pool voting

## Core Classes

### Tx Class
The main class for building governance transactions, extending QuickTx functionality.

### Governance Actions
- `InfoAction` - Information proposals
- `NewConstitution` - Constitution update proposals
- `NoConfidence` - No confidence proposals
- `ParameterChangeAction` - Protocol parameter changes
- `HardForkInitiationAction` - Hard fork initiation
- `TreasuryWithdrawalsAction` - Treasury withdrawal proposals
- `UpdateCommittee` - Committee update proposals

### Supporting Classes
- `Voter` - Represents different voter types (DRep, SPO, Committee)
- `Vote` - Vote options (Yes, No, Abstain)
- `Anchor` - Metadata anchor for proposals
- `GovActionId` - References to governance actions

## Usage Examples

### Setup

Create QuickTxBuilder and Account instances for governance operations:

```java
QuickTxBuilder quickTxBuilder = new QuickTxBuilder(backendService);

Account account = Account.createFromMnemonic(Networks.preprod(), "your mnemonic words");
String address = account.baseAddress();
```

In the examples below, `<anchor_datahash>` is a `byte[]`, the Blake2b-256 hash of the anchor document. If you have it as hex, use `HexUtil.decodeHexString(hash)`. Actions that follow an earlier action need `prevGovActionId` to be the last enacted action of that type on your network.

### DRep Management

Manage Delegated Representative (DRep) registration and operations:

#### Register DRep

Register an account as a Delegated Representative:

```java
var anchor = new Anchor("<anchor_url>", <anchor_datahash>);

Tx drepRegTx = new Tx()
        .registerDRep(account, anchor)
        .from(address);

Result<String> result = quickTxBuilder.compose(drepRegTx)
        .withSigner(SignerProviders.signerFrom(account))
        .withSigner(SignerProviders.signerFrom(account.drepHdKeyPair()))
        .completeAndWait(System.out::println);
```

#### Deregister DRep

Deregister an account as a DRep:

```java
Tx tx = new Tx()
        .unregisterDRep(account.drepCredential())
        .from(address);

Result<String> result = quickTxBuilder.compose(tx)
        .withSigner(SignerProviders.drepKeySignerFrom(account))
        .withSigner(SignerProviders.signerFrom(account))
        .completeAndWait(System.out::println);
```

#### Update DRep

Update DRep information (remove anchor):

```java
 Tx drepRegTx = new Tx()
        .updateDRep(account.drepCredential())
        .from(address);

Result<String> result = quickTxBuilder.compose(drepRegTx)
        .withSigner(SignerProviders.drepKeySignerFrom(account))
        .withSigner(SignerProviders.signerFrom(account))
        .completeAndWait(s -> System.out.println(s));
```

Update DRep information with a new anchor:

```java
var newAnchor = new Anchor("<anchor_url>", <anchor_datahash>);

Tx drepRegTx = new Tx()
        .updateDRep(account.drepCredential(), newAnchor)
        .from(address);

Result<String> result = quickTxBuilder.compose(drepRegTx)
        .withSigner(SignerProviders.drepKeySignerFrom(account))
        .withSigner(SignerProviders.signerFrom(account))
        .completeAndWait(s -> System.out.println(s));
```

### Governance Proposals

Create various types of governance proposals using the `createProposal()` method. Any account can create a proposal — a DRep key signature is **not** required.

#### Info Proposal

Create an information proposal:

```java
var govAction = new InfoAction();
var anchor = new Anchor("<anchor_url>", <anchor_datahash>);

Tx tx = new Tx()
        .createProposal(govAction, account.stakeAddress(), anchor)
        .from(address);

Result<String> result = quickTxBuilder.compose(tx)
        .withSigner(SignerProviders.signerFrom(account))
        .completeAndWait(s -> System.out.println(s));
```

#### Constitution Proposal

Create a new constitution proposal:

```java
var anchor = new Anchor("<anchor_url>", <anchor_datahash>);

var govAction = new NewConstitution();
govAction.setPrevGovActionId(new GovActionId("<prevGovActionTxHash>", prevGovActionIndex));
govAction.setConstitution(Constitution.builder()
        .anchor(anchor)
        .build());

Tx tx = new Tx()
        .createProposal(govAction, account.stakeAddress(), anchor)
        .from(address);

Result<String> result = quickTxBuilder.compose(tx)
        .withSigner(SignerProviders.signerFrom(account))
        .completeAndWait(s -> System.out.println(s));
```

#### No Confidence Proposal

Create a no confidence proposal:

```java
var noConfidence = new NoConfidence();
noConfidence.setPrevGovActionId(new GovActionId("<prevGovActionTxHash>", prevGovActionIndex));
var anchor = new Anchor("<anchor_url>", <anchor_datahash>);

Tx tx = new Tx()
        .createProposal(noConfidence, account.stakeAddress(), anchor)
        .from(address);

Result<String> result = quickTxBuilder.compose(tx)
        .withSigner(SignerProviders.signerFrom(account))
        .completeAndWait(s -> System.out.println(s));
```

#### Parameter Change Proposal

Create a protocol parameter change proposal:

```java
var parameterChange = new ParameterChangeAction();
parameterChange.setPrevGovActionId(new GovActionId("529736be1fac33431667f2b66231b7b66d4c7a3975319ddac7cfb17dcb5c4145", 0));
parameterChange.setProtocolParamUpdate(ProtocolParamUpdate.builder()
        .minPoolCost(ADAConversionUtil.adaToLovelace(100))
        .build());

var anchor = new Anchor("<anchor_url>", <anchor_datahash>);

Tx tx = new Tx()
        .createProposal(parameterChange, account.stakeAddress(), anchor)
        .from(address);

Result<String> result = quickTxBuilder.compose(tx)
        .withSigner(SignerProviders.signerFrom(account))
        .completeAndWait(s -> System.out.println(s));
```

#### Hard Fork Initiation Proposal

Create a hard fork initiation proposal:

```java
var hardforkInitiation = new HardForkInitiationAction();
hardforkInitiation.setPrevGovActionId(new GovActionId("416f7f01c548a85546aa5bbd155b34bb2802df68e08db4e843ef6da764cd8f7e", 0));
hardforkInitiation.setProtocolVersion(new ProtocolVersion(9, 0));

var anchor = new Anchor("<anchor_url>", <anchor_datahash>);

Tx tx = new Tx()
        .createProposal(hardforkInitiation, account.stakeAddress(), anchor)
        .from(address);

Result<String> result = quickTxBuilder.compose(tx)
        .withSigner(SignerProviders.signerFrom(account))
        .completeAndWait(s -> System.out.println(s));
```

#### Treasury Withdrawal Proposal

Create a treasury withdrawal proposal:
```java
var treasuryWithdrawalsAction = new TreasuryWithdrawalsAction();
treasuryWithdrawalsAction.addWithdrawal(new Withdrawal("<stake_address>", adaToLovelace(20)));

var anchor = new Anchor("<anchor_url>", <anchor_datahash>);

Tx tx = new Tx()
        .createProposal(treasuryWithdrawalsAction, account.stakeAddress(), anchor)
        .from(address);

Result<String> result = quickTxBuilder.compose(tx)
        .withSigner(SignerProviders.signerFrom(account))
        .completeAndWait(s -> System.out.println(s));
```

#### Update Committee Proposal

Create a committee update proposal:

```java
var updateCommittee = new UpdateCommittee();
updateCommittee.setPrevGovActionId(new GovActionId("b3ce0371310a07a797657d19453d953bb352b6841c2f5c5e0bd2557189ef5c3a", 0));
updateCommittee.setQuorumThreshold(new UnitInterval(BigInteger.valueOf(1), BigInteger.valueOf(3)));

var anchor = new Anchor("<anchor_url>", <anchor_datahash>);

Tx tx = new Tx()
        .createProposal(updateCommittee, account.stakeAddress(), anchor)
        .from(address);

Result<String> result = quickTxBuilder.compose(tx)
        .withSigner(SignerProviders.signerFrom(account))
        .completeAndWait(s -> System.out.println(s));
```

### Voting

Vote on governance proposals:

```java
var voter = new Voter(VoterType.DREP_KEY_HASH, account.drepCredential());
var govActionId = new GovActionId("5655fbb4ceafd34296fe58f6e3d28b8ff663a89e84aa0edd77bd02fe379cef4c", 0); //some gov action id

Tx tx = new Tx()
        .createVote(voter, govActionId, Vote.NO)
        .from(address);

Result<String> result = quickTxBuilder.compose(tx)
        .withSigner(SignerProviders.drepKeySignerFrom(account))
        .withSigner(SignerProviders.signerFrom(account))
        .completeAndWait(System.out::println);
```

### Vote Delegation

Delegate voting power to a DRep:

```java
DRep drep = GovId.toDrep(drepId); // the DRep's drep1... id

Tx tx = new Tx()
        .delegateVotingPowerTo(account.baseAddress(), drep)
        .from(address);

Result<String> result = quickTxBuilder.compose(tx)
        .withSigner(SignerProviders.stakeKeySignerFrom(account))
        .withSigner(SignerProviders.signerFrom(account))
        .completeAndWait(System.out::println);
```

---

# Programmable Tokens with CIP-113

Source: https://cardano-client.dev/learn/cip113-programmable-tokens/
Summary: Build a token that can't move without its issuer's approval: register, mint, transfer, seize and burn it on Preview.

A native Cardano token moves freely once it's minted. Nobody can block a transfer, freeze a holder or recover stolen funds, which rules out many regulated assets. [CIP-113](https://cips.cardano.org/cip/CIP-0113) adds rules without a hard fork: tokens sit at a shared script, and they change hands only if the token's own logic script approves.

In this tutorial you'll create a token that can't move without its issuer's signature, then take it through its whole life on the Preview testnet:

1. Register the token and mint 1,000 to Alice.
2. Watch a transfer fail because the issuer didn't approve it, then send an approved one to Bob.
3. Seize tokens from Bob without his signature.
4. Burn what you seized.

You finish with Alice holding 900 tokens, Bob holding 60, and a total supply of 960.

:::note[Version]
Programmable token support is available from **0.8.0-pre7**, and this tutorial was tested on that release. If the code doesn't compile on a newer release, check the programmable-token [release notes](https://github.com/bloxbean/cardano-client-lib/blob/master/programmable-token/RELEASE_NOTES.md).
:::

**You need:** Java 17+, and some experience with [QuickTx](/quicktx/overview/). If you haven't built a transaction with this library yet, start with [your first transaction](/learn/simple-transfer/).

## How CIP-113 works

Four ideas explain most of what follows.

**Smart wallet.** Programmable tokens never sit at an ordinary address. Each holder has a smart wallet: an address whose payment part is the shared `programmable_logic_base` script and whose stake part identifies the owner. Anyone can derive it from the owner's normal address, so a receiver doesn't have to set anything up. Once minted, tokens move only between smart wallets.

**Registry.** A shared on-chain linked list with one node per token. Each node records the scripts that govern that token, and anyone can add a node.

**Module.** Those scripts are the token's rules, and you write them. Together they form the token's module, which the CIP calls a *substandard*. The two terms mean the same thing.

| Script | Field in CCL | Runs when |
|---|---|---|
| Minting logic | `mintingLogicScript` | Tokens are minted or burned |
| Transfer logic | `transferLogicScript` | A holder moves or burns their own tokens |
| Third-party logic | `thirdPartyTransferLogicScript` | Someone acts on another holder's tokens, such as a seizure |

The CIP calls the minting logic `issuanceLogicScript`. A fourth script, `unfrackingLogicScript`, defaults to forbidden; see [Limits](#limits).

**Withdraw-zero.** Logic scripts run as a withdrawal of 0 lovelace from the script's own reward account. A script can then take part in a transaction without holding anything, but its reward account has to be registered first.

```text
                 shared protocol, already deployed
   +-----------------------------------------------------------+
   |  registry  -->  your token's node  -->  your logic scripts |
   +-----------------------------------------------------------+
                               |
                     checked on every move
                               |
   Alice's smart wallet  ------+------>  Bob's smart wallet
   (base script + Alice's key)           (base script + Bob's key)
```

You don't deploy any of this. The library ships descriptions of the public deployments as `Cip113Deployments.PREVIEW`, `PREPROD` and `MAINNET`. This tutorial uses Preview because that deployment already exists. A new Yaci DevKit devnet doesn't have one. You can deploy the protocol there with ordinary QuickTx transactions, but the library has no shortcut for it. If you really want to do that, see how [the library's end-to-end tests deploy it](https://github.com/bloxbean/cardano-client-lib/blob/master/programmable-token/src/it/java/com/bloxbean/cardano/client/programmabletoken/cip113/tx/Cip113Bootstrap.java), and pass the resulting description to `Cip113ProgrammableTokenService.create`.

When you build a transaction, the library finds the registry node, adds the protocol's reference inputs, writes its redeemers and sizes the min-ADA on each output. You only state what you want to happen.

:::note[Two addresses, one owner]
Alice's tokens sit in her smart wallet, but her fees and collateral come from her normal address, so a holder who sends tokens needs ADA there too.

The CIP lets an application key smart wallets by the owner's payment or stake credential, and the two choices give the same person different addresses. CCL defaults to `SmartWalletKey.PAYMENT`, which puts the owner's *payment* credential in the stake part of the address. Everyone holding or reading a token has to agree on the choice.
:::

## Set up your project

Add these dependencies, replacing `<version>` with the release you're using. `cardano-client-programmable-token` isn't part of the `cardano-client-lib` aggregate, so it has to be listed on its own.

```gradle
def cclVersion = '<version>'

dependencies {
    implementation "com.bloxbean.cardano:cardano-client-lib:$cclVersion"
    implementation "com.bloxbean.cardano:cardano-client-backend-blockfrost:$cclVersion"
    implementation "com.bloxbean.cardano:cardano-client-programmable-token:$cclVersion"
    implementation 'com.bloxbean.cardano:aiken-java-binding:0.1.0'
}
```

`aiken-java-binding` applies your script's parameter and evaluates scripts locally. It bundles native libraries for macOS, Windows and x86-64 Linux, but not ARM64 Linux. On ARM64 Linux, [use Scalus instead](#use-scalus-instead-of-aiken).

You also need a free [Blockfrost](https://blockfrost.io) project for Preview and a funded wallet. Create a wallet with this class:

```java
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.account.Account;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.common.model.Networks;

public class CreateWallet {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Account account = new Account(Networks.preview());
        System.out.println("Mnemonic: " + account.mnemonic());
        System.out.println("Fund this address: " + account.baseAddress());
    }
}
```

Send at least 50 tADA to the printed address from the [testnet faucet](https://docs.cardano.org/cardano-testnets/tools/faucet), selecting Preview. Then export your settings:

```bash
export BF_PROJECT_ID=<your Blockfrost Preview project id>
export TUTORIAL_MNEMONIC="<the words printed above>"
```

## Step 1: Connect to the deployment

The code below derives three accounts from your mnemonic. The issuer is account 0, the address you funded. Alice and Bob are accounts 1 and 2.

```java
public class IssuerApprovedToken {

    /** issuer_approved.issuer_approved.withdraw from plutus.json, before the issuer is applied. */
    private static final String COMPILED_CODE =
            "5895010100229800aba2aba1aab9faab9eaab9dab9a9bae002488888896600264646644b3001"
            + "3370e900218039baa00189991198008009bac300c300d300d300d300d300d300d300d300d30"
            + "0a3754601800c601460106ea8004896600200314a115980099b8f375c601800200f14a31330"
            + "02002300d0014020805a2c8030c020004c020c024004c020004c010dd5004452689b2b200401";

    private static final String ASSET_NAME = "TutorialToken";

    /** How long to wait for a submitted transaction to land in a block. */
    private static final Duration CONFIRM_TIMEOUT = Duration.ofMinutes(5);

    /** How long to let the backend's UTxO view catch up after a confirmed transaction. */
    private static final Duration SETTLE_TIME = Duration.ofSeconds(60);

    private final BackendService backend;
    private final Network network;
    private final Account issuer;
    private final Account alice;
    private final Account bob;

    private final Cip113ProgrammableTokenService tokens;
    private final Cip113ProtocolService protocol;
    private final Address issuerAddress;

    private PlutusScript logicScript;
    private Credential logic;
    private String policyId;

    public IssuerApprovedToken(BackendService backend, Cip113ProgrammableTokenService tokens,
                               Network network, Account issuer, Account alice, Account bob) {
        this.backend = backend;
        this.network = network;
        this.issuer = issuer;
        this.alice = alice;
        this.bob = bob;
        this.issuerAddress = new Address(issuer.baseAddress());
        this.tokens = tokens;
        this.protocol = tokens.advanced();
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        String projectId = System.getenv("BF_PROJECT_ID");
        String mnemonic = System.getenv("TUTORIAL_MNEMONIC");
        Network network = Networks.preview();

        BackendService backend = new BFBackendService(Constants.BLOCKFROST_PREVIEW_URL, projectId);

        // One mnemonic, three separate accounts: the issuer and two holders.
        Account issuer = Account.createFromMnemonic(network, mnemonic, 0, 0);
        Account alice = Account.createFromMnemonic(network, mnemonic, 1, 0);
        Account bob = Account.createFromMnemonic(network, mnemonic, 2, 0);

        Cip113ProgrammableTokenService tokens =
                Cip113ProgrammableTokenService.create(backend, Cip113Deployments.PREVIEW);

        new IssuerApprovedToken(backend, tokens, network, issuer, alice, bob).run();
    }

    public void run() throws Exception {
        prepareLogicScript(); // Needed on every run. It submits nothing.

        // Run 1: fund Alice, register the token and mint.
        // These work once per wallet, so comment them out before run 2.
        fundAlice();
        registerRewardAccount();
        registerAndMint();
        printBalances("after mint");

        // Run 2: uncomment to try a transfer.
        // transferWithoutApproval();
        // transfer();
        // printBalances("after transfer");

        // Run 3: uncomment to seize and burn, after commenting out run 2.
        // seize();
        // printBalances("after seizure");
        // burn();
        // printBalances("final");
    }

    // The methods below go here.
}
```

`Cip113ProgrammableTokenService` is the entry point. `tokens.extension()` plugs the protocol into QuickTx, and `tokens.advanced()` gives you the read side used throughout this tutorial.

The sections below add one method each to this class, and the [complete class](#run-it) is at the end.

## Step 2: Write the token's rule

This token has a single rule, written in [Aiken](https://aiken-lang.org): the issuer must have signed.

```rust
use aiken/collection/list
use aiken/crypto.{VerificationKeyHash}
use cardano/address.{Credential}
use cardano/transaction.{Transaction}

/// Passes only when `issuer` signed the transaction.
validator issuer_approved(issuer: VerificationKeyHash) {
  withdraw(_redeemer: Data, _account: Credential, tx: Transaction) {
    list.has(tx.extra_signatories, issuer)
  }

  else(_) {
    fail
  }
}
```

You don't need Aiken installed. The compiled validator is the `COMPILED_CODE` constant in the class above, built with Aiken v1.1.23 and stdlib v3.0.0.

One script serves all three roles here, so there's only one reward account to register. A real token would usually have a separate script for each role.

`issuer` is a parameter, so every issuer gets a different script hash. That matters because a token's policy id is derived from its minting script's hash. You don't choose the policy id, and two tokens with the same minting script would be the same token. Your parameterized script gives you a policy nobody else in the shared registry has.

```java
private void prepareLogicScript() throws Exception {
    byte[] issuerKeyHash = issuer.hdKeyPair().getPublicKey().getKeyHash();

    String applied = AikenScriptUtil.applyParamToScript(
            ListPlutusData.of(BytesPlutusData.of(issuerKeyHash)), COMPILED_CODE);
    logicScript = PlutusBlueprintUtil.getPlutusScriptFromCompiledCode(applied, PlutusVersion.v3);
    logic = Credential.fromScript(logicScript.getPolicyId());

    // Nothing on chain has used this script yet, so no backend can serve it.
    protocol.scripts().register(logicScript);

    policyId = value(protocol.derivePolicyId(logic));
    System.out.println("Logic script : " + logicScript.getPolicyId());
    System.out.println("Policy id    : " + policyId);
}
```

The `register` call is needed because a backend can serve a script only after the chain has revealed it, and yours hasn't been used yet.

## Step 3: Fund Alice and register the reward account

Alice needs ADA at her normal address for fees and collateral:

```java
private void fundAlice() {
    Tx tx = new Tx()
            .payToAddress(alice.baseAddress(), Amount.ada(30))
            .from(issuer.baseAddress());

    check("Fund alice", new QuickTxBuilder(backend)
            .compose(tx)
            .withSigner(SignerProviders.signerFrom(issuer))
            .completeAndWait(CONFIRM_TIMEOUT));
}
```

Every submission in this tutorial goes through `check`, which stops unless the transaction is confirmed and then pauses:

```java
private static void check(String step, TxResult result) {
    if (!result.isSuccessful())
        throw new IllegalStateException(step + " failed: " + result.getResponse());
    if (result.getTxStatus() != TxStatus.CONFIRMED)
        throw new IllegalStateException(step + " not confirmed (" + result.getTxStatus() + "): " + result.getValue());
    System.out.printf("%-12s : %s%n", step, result.getValue());
    settle();
}

private static void settle() {
    try {
        Thread.sleep(SETTLE_TIME.toMillis());
    } catch (InterruptedException e) {
        Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
        throw new IllegalStateException(e);
    }
}
```

Both checks matter on a public network:

- **Confirmation.** `completeAndWait()` waits 60 seconds by default. If the transaction hasn't landed by then, the result still reports `isSuccessful()`, with the status `TIMEOUT`. Blocks can be slow on Preview, where one of our test transactions took about two minutes, so this code waits up to five minutes and accepts only `CONFIRMED`.
- **The pause.** Blockfrost's UTxO queries can lag behind a confirmed transaction: we measured anywhere from 1 to 37 seconds on Preview. Without the pause, the next transaction can pick a UTxO that was just spent.

This keeps the tutorial simple, but a production application should chain transactions properly, for example with [TxFlow](/txflow/overview/).

Next, register the script's reward account so that withdraw-zero can run it. This needs no script witness. The check for `StakeKeyRegistered` lets you run this step again safely.

```java
private void registerRewardAccount() {
    String rewardAddress = AddressProvider.getRewardAddress(logic, network).toBech32();

    TxResult result = new QuickTxBuilder(backend)
            .compose(new Tx()
                    .registerStakeAddress(rewardAddress)
                    .from(issuer.baseAddress()))
            .withSigner(SignerProviders.signerFrom(issuer))
            .completeAndWait(CONFIRM_TIMEOUT);

    if (!result.isSuccessful() && result.getResponse().contains("StakeKeyRegistered")) {
        System.out.println("Reward account already registered");
        return;
    }
    check("Reward acct", result);
}
```

## Step 4: Register the token and mint

Every programmable-token transaction goes through this helper:

```java
private QuickTxBuilder.TxContext builder(Tx tx, Account sender) {
    return new QuickTxBuilder(backend)
            .withExtension(tokens.extension())
            .compose(tx)
            .withSigner(SignerProviders.signerFrom(sender))
            .withTxEvaluator(new AikenTransactionEvaluator(backend));
}
```

`withExtension` is what turns verbs like `register` and `mint` into a real transaction. `withTxEvaluator` runs the scripts locally, so a script failure stops the build before anything is submitted.

Now register the token and mint its first supply in one transaction:

```java
private void registerAndMint() {
    RegistryNodeSpec spec = RegistryNodeSpec.builder()
            .mintingLogicScript(logic)
            .transferLogicScript(logic)
            .thirdPartyTransferLogicScript(logic)
            .build();

    ProgrammableTokenTx tx = new ProgrammableTokenTx()
            .from(issuer.baseAddress())
            .register("tutorial", Cip113Registration.from(spec), PlutusData.unit())
            .mint(ProgrammableTokenPolicyRef.named("tutorial"), alice.baseAddress(),
                    List.of(new Asset(ASSET_NAME, BigInteger.valueOf(1000))),
                    PlutusData.unit(), null);

    check("Register", builder(tx, issuer)
            .withRequiredSigners(issuerAddress)
            .completeAndWait(CONFIRM_TIMEOUT));
}
```

- `RegistryNodeSpec` names the scripts for each role.
- `ProgrammableTokenPolicyRef.named("tutorial")` points the mint at the registration in the same transaction. The name exists only inside this transaction. Later mints use the literal policy id.
- `alice.baseAddress()` is Alice's normal address. The library maps it to her smart wallet, so the tokens land there.
- `PlutusData.unit()` is the redeemer. This validator ignores its redeemer.
- `withRequiredSigners` declares the issuer. A script sees only the signers a transaction declares, so `tx.extra_signatories` would otherwise be empty.

Registration spends a node of the shared registry, so it can collide with someone else registering at the same moment. If that happens, run it again.

## Step 5: Check the balances

```java
private void printBalances(String label) {
    System.out.printf("%-15s alice=%s bob=%s issuer=%s%n", label,
            balance(alice), balance(bob), balance(issuer));
}

private BigInteger balance(Account holder) {
    String unit = policyId + HexUtil.encodeHexString(ASSET_NAME.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
    return value(protocol.getProgrammableBalance(new Address(holder.baseAddress()))).stream()
            .filter(amount -> unit.equals(amount.getUnit()))
            .map(Amount::getQuantity)
            .reduce(BigInteger.ZERO, BigInteger::add);
}
```

`getProgrammableBalance` takes the owner's normal address and reads their smart wallet. It returns only tokens that are in the registry. Other calls on `protocol` you may find useful are `smartWalletAddress`, `isProgrammable` and `getRegistryNode`.

After the mint you'll see:

```text
after mint      alice=1000 bob=0 issuer=0
```

## Step 6: Try a transfer without approval

Alice tries to send 100 tokens to Bob, signing alone:

```java
private void transferWithoutApproval() {
    ProgrammableTokenTx tx = new ProgrammableTokenTx()
            .from(alice.baseAddress())
            .transfer(bob.baseAddress(), Amount.asset(policyId, ASSET_NAME, 100), PlutusData.unit());

    try {
        builder(tx, alice).completeAndWait();
    } catch (TxBuildException e) {
        System.out.println("Rejected     : " + e.getMessage());
        return;
    }
    throw new IllegalStateException("The transfer should not have passed without the issuer");
}
```

The library declares Alice as a required signer because her wallet is being spent, and that satisfies the protocol. But the token's transfer logic also runs, finds no issuer signature and fails. Evaluation stops the build, so nothing is submitted and no fee or collateral is at risk.

The failure is thrown as a `TxBuildException` with this message:

```text
Rejected     : Error while evaluating script cost
```

If you have an SLF4J provider on the classpath, the evaluator also logs the reason. `tag: "Withdraw"` tells you that a withdraw-zero script said no:

```text
AIKEN: RedeemerError { tag: "Withdraw", index: 2, err: Machine(EvaluationFailure, ...) }
```

## Step 7: Send an approved transfer

The same transaction goes through once the issuer approves it. Both parts matter: `withRequiredSigners` declares the issuer, and `withSigner` adds the signature.

```java
private void transfer() {
    ProgrammableTokenTx tx = new ProgrammableTokenTx()
            .from(alice.baseAddress())
            .transfer(bob.baseAddress(), Amount.asset(policyId, ASSET_NAME, 100), PlutusData.unit());

    check("Transfer", builder(tx, alice)
            .withRequiredSigners(issuerAddress)
            .withSigner(SignerProviders.signerFrom(issuer))
            .completeAndWait(CONFIRM_TIMEOUT));
}
```

```text
after transfer  alice=900 bob=100 issuer=0
```

## Step 8: Seize tokens

Now the issuer takes 40 tokens from Bob. Bob doesn't sign, and he doesn't need any ADA either.

```java
private void seize() {
    ProgrammableTokenTx tx = new ProgrammableTokenTx()
            .from(issuer.baseAddress())
            .thirdPartyTransfer(bob.baseAddress(), issuer.baseAddress(),
                    Amount.asset(policyId, ASSET_NAME, 40), PlutusData.unit());

    check("Seize", builder(tx, issuer)
            .withRequiredSigners(issuerAddress)
            .completeAndWait(CONFIRM_TIMEOUT));
}
```

`thirdPartyTransfer` takes the holder, the receiver, the amount and a redeemer. The library selects Bob's UTxOs, spends them under the token's third-party logic, and keeps whatever isn't seized in his smart wallet.

Unlike a transfer, this verb declares no signer for you, so `withRequiredSigners` is what makes the issuer's signature visible to the script.

```text
after seizure   alice=900 bob=60 issuer=40
```

:::danger[Holders can't refuse a seizure]
Whoever the third-party logic accepts can take tokens from any smart wallet. If a token's third-party logic always succeeds, **anyone can take anyone's tokens**. The library can't prevent that, because it's how the token was designed. Before you accept a token, read its rules with `protocol.getRegistryNode(policyId)`.
:::

## Step 9: Burn tokens

The issuer now burns the 40 seized tokens:

```java
private void burn() {
    ProgrammableTokenTx tx = new ProgrammableTokenTx()
            .from(issuer.baseAddress())
            .burn(policyId, List.of(new Asset(ASSET_NAME, BigInteger.valueOf(40))),
                    BurnAuthorization.of(PlutusData.unit(), PlutusData.unit()));

    check("Burn", builder(tx, issuer).completeAndWait(CONFIRM_TIMEOUT));
}
```

A burn has its own verb because it needs two approvals: the transfer logic spends the tokens from the wallet, and the minting logic approves the negative mint. `BurnAuthorization` carries a redeemer for each. This token uses one script for both roles, and that script runs once, so you pass the same value twice.

There's no `withRequiredSigners` here. The issuer is spending their own smart wallet, so the library already declares them as the owner, and that's the same key the script checks.

```text
final           alice=900 bob=60 issuer=0
```

## Run it

Here is the complete class, ready to copy. It runs in stages, so that you can try your first mint before going further:

1. **Run it as it is** to register the token and mint 1,000 units to Alice.
2. **In `run()`, comment out the run 1 lines and uncomment the run 2 lines**, then run it again to transfer to Bob. Run 2 also shows a transfer being rejected without the issuer's approval.
3. **Comment out the run 2 lines and uncomment the run 3 lines**, then run it again to seize and burn.

<details open>
<summary>IssuerApprovedToken.java</summary>

```java
package tutorial;

import com.bloxbean.cardano.aiken.AikenScriptUtil;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.aiken.AikenTransactionEvaluator;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.account.Account;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.address.Address;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.address.AddressProvider;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.address.Credential;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.api.model.Amount;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.api.model.Result;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.backend.api.BackendService;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.backend.blockfrost.common.Constants;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.backend.blockfrost.service.BFBackendService;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.common.model.Network;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.common.model.Networks;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.function.exception.TxBuildException;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.function.helper.SignerProviders;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.plutus.blueprint.PlutusBlueprintUtil;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.plutus.blueprint.model.PlutusVersion;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.plutus.spec.BytesPlutusData;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.plutus.spec.ListPlutusData;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.plutus.spec.PlutusData;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.plutus.spec.PlutusScript;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.programmabletoken.BurnAuthorization;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.programmabletoken.ProgrammableTokenPolicyRef;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.programmabletoken.ProgrammableTokenTx;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.programmabletoken.cip113.Cip113Deployments;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.programmabletoken.cip113.Cip113ProgrammableTokenService;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.programmabletoken.cip113.Cip113ProtocolService;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.programmabletoken.cip113.Cip113Registration;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.programmabletoken.cip113.tx.RegistryNodeSpec;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.quicktx.QuickTxBuilder;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.quicktx.Tx;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.quicktx.TxResult;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.quicktx.TxStatus;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.transaction.spec.Asset;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.util.HexUtil;

import java.math.BigInteger;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.time.Duration;
import java.util.List;

public class IssuerApprovedToken {

    /** issuer_approved.issuer_approved.withdraw from plutus.json, before the issuer is applied. */
    private static final String COMPILED_CODE =
            "5895010100229800aba2aba1aab9faab9eaab9dab9a9bae002488888896600264646644b3001"
            + "3370e900218039baa00189991198008009bac300c300d300d300d300d300d300d300d300d30"
            + "0a3754601800c601460106ea8004896600200314a115980099b8f375c601800200f14a31330"
            + "02002300d0014020805a2c8030c020004c020c024004c020004c010dd5004452689b2b200401";

    private static final String ASSET_NAME = "TutorialToken";

    /** How long to wait for a submitted transaction to land in a block. */
    private static final Duration CONFIRM_TIMEOUT = Duration.ofMinutes(5);

    /** How long to let the backend's UTxO view catch up after a confirmed transaction. */
    private static final Duration SETTLE_TIME = Duration.ofSeconds(60);

    private final BackendService backend;
    private final Network network;
    private final Account issuer;
    private final Account alice;
    private final Account bob;

    private final Cip113ProgrammableTokenService tokens;
    private final Cip113ProtocolService protocol;
    private final Address issuerAddress;

    private PlutusScript logicScript;
    private Credential logic;
    private String policyId;

    public IssuerApprovedToken(BackendService backend, Cip113ProgrammableTokenService tokens,
                               Network network, Account issuer, Account alice, Account bob) {
        this.backend = backend;
        this.network = network;
        this.issuer = issuer;
        this.alice = alice;
        this.bob = bob;
        this.issuerAddress = new Address(issuer.baseAddress());
        this.tokens = tokens;
        this.protocol = tokens.advanced();
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        String projectId = System.getenv("BF_PROJECT_ID");
        String mnemonic = System.getenv("TUTORIAL_MNEMONIC");
        Network network = Networks.preview();

        BackendService backend = new BFBackendService(Constants.BLOCKFROST_PREVIEW_URL, projectId);

        // One mnemonic, three separate accounts: the issuer and two holders.
        Account issuer = Account.createFromMnemonic(network, mnemonic, 0, 0);
        Account alice = Account.createFromMnemonic(network, mnemonic, 1, 0);
        Account bob = Account.createFromMnemonic(network, mnemonic, 2, 0);

        Cip113ProgrammableTokenService tokens =
                Cip113ProgrammableTokenService.create(backend, Cip113Deployments.PREVIEW);

        new IssuerApprovedToken(backend, tokens, network, issuer, alice, bob).run();
    }

    public void run() throws Exception {
        prepareLogicScript(); // Needed on every run. It submits nothing.

        // Run 1: fund Alice, register the token and mint.
        // These work once per wallet, so comment them out before run 2.
        fundAlice();
        registerRewardAccount();
        registerAndMint();
        printBalances("after mint");

        // Run 2: uncomment to try a transfer.
        // transferWithoutApproval();
        // transfer();
        // printBalances("after transfer");

        // Run 3: uncomment to seize and burn, after commenting out run 2.
        // seize();
        // printBalances("after seizure");
        // burn();
        // printBalances("final");
    }

    // -- Step: the token's logic script

    private void prepareLogicScript() throws Exception {
        byte[] issuerKeyHash = issuer.hdKeyPair().getPublicKey().getKeyHash();

        String applied = AikenScriptUtil.applyParamToScript(
                ListPlutusData.of(BytesPlutusData.of(issuerKeyHash)), COMPILED_CODE);
        logicScript = PlutusBlueprintUtil.getPlutusScriptFromCompiledCode(applied, PlutusVersion.v3);
        logic = Credential.fromScript(logicScript.getPolicyId());

        // Nothing on chain has used this script yet, so no backend can serve it.
        protocol.scripts().register(logicScript);

        policyId = value(protocol.derivePolicyId(logic));
        System.out.println("Logic script : " + logicScript.getPolicyId());
        System.out.println("Policy id    : " + policyId);
    }

    private void fundAlice() {
        Tx tx = new Tx()
                .payToAddress(alice.baseAddress(), Amount.ada(30))
                .from(issuer.baseAddress());

        check("Fund alice", new QuickTxBuilder(backend)
                .compose(tx)
                .withSigner(SignerProviders.signerFrom(issuer))
                .completeAndWait(CONFIRM_TIMEOUT));
    }

    // -- Step: withdraw-zero needs a registered reward account

    private void registerRewardAccount() {
        String rewardAddress = AddressProvider.getRewardAddress(logic, network).toBech32();

        TxResult result = new QuickTxBuilder(backend)
                .compose(new Tx()
                        .registerStakeAddress(rewardAddress)
                        .from(issuer.baseAddress()))
                .withSigner(SignerProviders.signerFrom(issuer))
                .completeAndWait(CONFIRM_TIMEOUT);

        if (!result.isSuccessful() && result.getResponse().contains("StakeKeyRegistered")) {
            System.out.println("Reward account already registered");
            return;
        }
        check("Reward acct", result);
    }

    // -- Step: register the token and mint its first supply

    private void registerAndMint() {
        RegistryNodeSpec spec = RegistryNodeSpec.builder()
                .mintingLogicScript(logic)
                .transferLogicScript(logic)
                .thirdPartyTransferLogicScript(logic)
                .build();

        ProgrammableTokenTx tx = new ProgrammableTokenTx()
                .from(issuer.baseAddress())
                .register("tutorial", Cip113Registration.from(spec), PlutusData.unit())
                .mint(ProgrammableTokenPolicyRef.named("tutorial"), alice.baseAddress(),
                        List.of(new Asset(ASSET_NAME, BigInteger.valueOf(1000))),
                        PlutusData.unit(), null);

        check("Register", builder(tx, issuer)
                .withRequiredSigners(issuerAddress)
                .completeAndWait(CONFIRM_TIMEOUT));
    }

    // -- Step: a transfer without the issuer's signature

    private void transferWithoutApproval() {
        ProgrammableTokenTx tx = new ProgrammableTokenTx()
                .from(alice.baseAddress())
                .transfer(bob.baseAddress(), Amount.asset(policyId, ASSET_NAME, 100), PlutusData.unit());

        try {
            builder(tx, alice).completeAndWait();
        } catch (TxBuildException e) {
            System.out.println("Rejected     : " + e.getMessage());
            return;
        }
        throw new IllegalStateException("The transfer should not have passed without the issuer");
    }

    // -- Step: the same transfer, approved

    private void transfer() {
        ProgrammableTokenTx tx = new ProgrammableTokenTx()
                .from(alice.baseAddress())
                .transfer(bob.baseAddress(), Amount.asset(policyId, ASSET_NAME, 100), PlutusData.unit());

        check("Transfer", builder(tx, alice)
                .withRequiredSigners(issuerAddress)
                .withSigner(SignerProviders.signerFrom(issuer))
                .completeAndWait(CONFIRM_TIMEOUT));
    }

    // -- Step: seize tokens without the holder's signature

    private void seize() {
        ProgrammableTokenTx tx = new ProgrammableTokenTx()
                .from(issuer.baseAddress())
                .thirdPartyTransfer(bob.baseAddress(), issuer.baseAddress(),
                        Amount.asset(policyId, ASSET_NAME, 40), PlutusData.unit());

        check("Seize", builder(tx, issuer)
                .withRequiredSigners(issuerAddress)
                .completeAndWait(CONFIRM_TIMEOUT));
    }

    // -- Step: burn

    private void burn() {
        ProgrammableTokenTx tx = new ProgrammableTokenTx()
                .from(issuer.baseAddress())
                .burn(policyId, List.of(new Asset(ASSET_NAME, BigInteger.valueOf(40))),
                        BurnAuthorization.of(PlutusData.unit(), PlutusData.unit()));

        check("Burn", builder(tx, issuer).completeAndWait(CONFIRM_TIMEOUT));
    }

    // -- Helpers

    private QuickTxBuilder.TxContext builder(Tx tx, Account sender) {
        return new QuickTxBuilder(backend)
                .withExtension(tokens.extension())
                .compose(tx)
                .withSigner(SignerProviders.signerFrom(sender))
                .withTxEvaluator(new AikenTransactionEvaluator(backend));
    }

    private void printBalances(String label) {
        System.out.printf("%-15s alice=%s bob=%s issuer=%s%n", label,
                balance(alice), balance(bob), balance(issuer));
    }

    private BigInteger balance(Account holder) {
        String unit = policyId + HexUtil.encodeHexString(ASSET_NAME.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
        return value(protocol.getProgrammableBalance(new Address(holder.baseAddress()))).stream()
                .filter(amount -> unit.equals(amount.getUnit()))
                .map(Amount::getQuantity)
                .reduce(BigInteger.ZERO, BigInteger::add);
    }

    private static void check(String step, TxResult result) {
        if (!result.isSuccessful())
            throw new IllegalStateException(step + " failed: " + result.getResponse());
        if (result.getTxStatus() != TxStatus.CONFIRMED)
            throw new IllegalStateException(step + " not confirmed (" + result.getTxStatus() + "): " + result.getValue());
        System.out.printf("%-12s : %s%n", step, result.getValue());
        settle();
    }

    private static void settle() {
        try {
            Thread.sleep(SETTLE_TIME.toMillis());
        } catch (InterruptedException e) {
            Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
            throw new IllegalStateException(e);
        }
    }

    private static <T> T value(Result<T> result) {
        if (!result.isSuccessful()) throw new IllegalStateException(result.getResponse());
        return result.getValue();
    }
}
```

</details>

On Preview, the three runs print something like this, with your own hashes. Each run starts with the `Logic script` and `Policy id` lines, which are the same every time.

```text
Logic script : 88b22cd904b2aee70c4401e1946d7f9dc64f994f2cd78d63506659e7
Policy id    : 6eea33c0c1b7604ff56e3906ed5b4ebac98791beec17b9d6a6eb30cb
Fund alice   : 31035ba6028e7503a46855b76ee670cb40e9e250d245156c6bfc9dc305363c4c
Reward acct  : d1eb35c75cea0267263af683b753e9f259a2b0278edc45af4baddcdcb5dfff26
Register     : 1888b7ded91938a781bdaf2b190d0b0d2a7209c6c7266620c35da43276019a76
after mint      alice=1000 bob=0 issuer=0

Rejected     : Error while evaluating script cost
Transfer     : dd17f6d0ab4bd396d0e813f2266681b974ca3f97204c84ad37b34047fc11bcc4
after transfer  alice=900 bob=100 issuer=0

Seize        : bffa140c42094db1409d568f1bcb8f5fe56c68b4046b05a1dc155f0055d34db9
after seizure   alice=900 bob=60 issuer=40
Burn         : 2b93d79a3a754975507ded23ff6763bd9ef94af5ec440660722c8c3291957b25
final           alice=900 bob=60 issuer=0
```

The whole run cost about 7 tADA from the issuer and 1.6 tADA from Alice, on top of the 30 tADA the issuer sends her.

You can look up each transaction hash in a [Preview explorer](https://preview.cardanoscan.io).

Run 1 works once per mnemonic, because the token stays registered. To start again from run 1, create a new wallet. With the pauses, our Preview run took about ten minutes.

## Use Scalus instead of Aiken

[Scalus](/smart-contracts/scalus/) can do both jobs that Aiken Java Binding does here, and it also runs on ARM64 Linux. Replace the `aiken-java-binding` dependency with `org.scalus:scalus-bloxbean-cardano-client-lib_3:1.4.1`, then change two places.

Apply the parameter in `prepareLogicScript`:

```java
PlutusScript unapplied = PlutusBlueprintUtil.getPlutusScriptFromCompiledCode(COMPILED_CODE, PlutusVersion.v3);
String applied = ScalusScriptUtils.applyParamsToScript(unapplied.getCborHex(), BytesPlutusData.of(issuerKeyHash));
logicScript = PlutusV3Script.builder().type("PlutusScriptV3").cborHex(applied).build();
```

Evaluate scripts in `builder`, with `params` from `backend.getEpochService().getProtocolParameters().getValue()`:

```java
.withTxEvaluator(new ScalusTransactionEvaluator(
        params, new DefaultUtxoSupplier(backend.getUtxoService()),
        new ScriptServiceSupplier(backend.getScriptService())));
```

The parameter gives the same script hash either way, so a token registered with one tool works with the other.

## What you built

| Action | Verb | Who signs | Logic that runs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Register and mint | `register`, `mint` | Issuer | Minting |
| Transfer | `transfer` | Holder and issuer | Transfer |
| Seize | `thirdPartyTransfer` | Issuer | Third-party |
| Burn | `burn` | Holder (here, the issuer) | Transfer and minting |

The "issuer" requirement comes from your script, not from the protocol. A different script gives you different rules, and the Java code barely changes.

## Troubleshooting

| What you see | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `All inputs are spent. Transaction has probably already been included` | The backend returned a UTxO that a confirmed transaction had already spent | Wait and retry, or increase `SETTLE_TIME` |
| `... not confirmed (TIMEOUT): <hash>` | The transaction didn't land within `CONFIRM_TIMEOUT`, and it may still land | Look up the hash in an explorer. Run again once it has landed, using a new wallet if the token is already registered, and increase `CONFIRM_TIMEOUT` |
| `No covering registry node for policy ...` | The token is already registered, so `registerAndMint()` can't run again on this wallet. Comment out the run 1 lines, or create a new wallet. |
| `Could not resolve the minting logic script ...` | The chain hasn't revealed your script, and you didn't hand it over | Call `protocol.scripts().register(script)` before building |
| `ConwayWithdrawalsMissingAccounts` in the submit response | The script's reward account isn't registered | Run [Step 3](#step-3-fund-alice-and-register-the-reward-account) |
| `No covering registry node for policy ...` | That policy is already registered, usually because you ran the story twice | Skip `register`, or create a new wallet |
| `Error while evaluating script cost` | A script rejected the transaction, usually because the issuer isn't declared | Add `withRequiredSigners(issuerAddress)` |
| `MissingVKeyWitnessesUTXOW` in the submit response | A signer was declared but didn't sign | Add the matching `withSigner(...)` |
| `Not enough plain ADA to fund this transaction safely` | The sender's normal address has too little ADA in ADA-only UTxOs | Send ADA to that address; about 4.5 ADA covered a transfer in testing |
| `Smart wallet ... does not hold enough` | The sender's smart wallet doesn't have those tokens | Check `getProgrammableBalance` |

## Limits

- **Logic credentials must be scripts.** Registrations and updates that name a verification key are refused, so you can't create a token this library couldn't operate.
- **Unfracking isn't supported.** `unfrack(...)` throws `UnsupportedOperationException` on every deployment, and none of the public deployments can unfrack.
- **A third-party transaction acts on one policy,** and owner transfers and burns can't share it.
- **One `Tx` per transaction.** Write all programmable-token operations of a transaction in a single `Tx`, because splitting them across `compose(tx1, tx2)` is refused.
- **Each programmable output holds one policy,** and inline datums are limited by the deployment's `max_inline_datum_bytes`.
- **Protocol upgrades and authority changes** aren't authored by this library.

## Next steps

- Give each role its own script. For example, keep transfers open and add a denylist using `globalStateCs` on `RegistryNodeSpec`.
- Read the [programmable-token README](https://github.com/bloxbean/cardano-client-lib/blob/master/programmable-token/README.md) for `thirdPartyBurn`, `updateRegistry`, inline datums and custom deployments.
- Store these transactions as YAML with [TxPlan](/txplan/overview/). Programmable-token plans go through `tokens.txPlanCodec()`, not plain `TxPlan.toYaml()`.
- Run several steps in sequence with [TxFlow](/txflow/overview/), registering the extension on the runtime.

---

# Minting an NFT

Source: https://cardano-client.dev/learn/minting-an-nft/
Summary: Mint a one-of-a-kind token with CIP-25 metadata and a time-locked policy, using QuickTx.

An NFT on Cardano is a native token with a quantity of 1, whose policy can't mint any more. In this tutorial you'll create that policy, describe the token with CIP-25 metadata, mint it on the Preview testnet and find it in your wallet.

**Before you start**, follow [Your first transaction](/learn/simple-transfer/) to [create an account](/learn/simple-transfer/#create-sender-and-receiver-accounts), fund it from the [faucet](/learn/simple-transfer/#topup-sender-account-with-test-ada) and get a Blockfrost project id. To use a local network instead, see [Test locally with Yaci DevKit](/learn/test-with-yaci-devkit/). The [dependencies](/start-here/installation/) are `cardano-client-lib` and `cardano-client-backend-blockfrost`.

The code reads your settings from the environment:

```bash
export BF_PROJECT_ID=<your Blockfrost Preview project id>
export TUTORIAL_MNEMONIC="<your 24 words>"
```

## Step 1: Create the policy

A token's policy decides who can mint it and when. A policy id is the hash of its script, so a new script gives you a new policy.

```java
long deadline = backend.getBlockService().getLatestBlock().getValue().getSlot() + 3600;
Keys policyKeys = KeyGenUtil.generateKey();
ScriptAll policyScript = new ScriptAll()
        .addScript(ScriptPubkey.create(policyKeys.getVkey()))
        .addScript(new RequireTimeBefore(deadline));
Policy policy = new Policy(policyScript, List.of(policyKeys.getSkey()));
```

`ScriptAll` means both conditions must hold: the new key signs, and the transaction is valid only before `deadline`. One slot is one second on Preview, so that's one hour from now.

This is what makes the token one of a kind. A quantity of 1 alone doesn't: without the deadline, the key holder could mint the same token again.

## Step 2: Describe the token

Wallets and explorers read an NFT's name and image from [CIP-25](/standards/cip25/) metadata, which you attach to the minting transaction.

```java
Asset nftAsset = new Asset("MyFirstNft", BigInteger.ONE);
NFT nft = NFT.create()
        .assetName(nftAsset.getName())
        .name("My First NFT")
        .image("ipfs://QmYwAPJzv5CZsnA625s3Xf2nemtYgPpHdWEz79ojWnPbdG")
        .description("Minted with Cardano Client Lib");
NFTMetadata metadata = NFTMetadata.create().addNFT(policy.getPolicyId(), nft);
```

Replace `image` with the location of your own file. This sample points to a placeholder on IPFS.

## Step 3: Mint

```java
Tx tx = new Tx()
        .mintAssets(policy.getPolicyScript(), nftAsset, minter.baseAddress())
        .attachMetadata(metadata)
        .from(minter.baseAddress());

TxResult result = new QuickTxBuilder(backend)
        .compose(tx)
        .validTo(deadline)
        .withSigner(SignerProviders.signerFrom(minter))
        .withSigner(SignerProviders.signerFrom(policy))
        .completeAndWait(Duration.ofMinutes(5));
```

- `validTo(deadline)` is required. The script accepts a transaction only if it declares that it expires before the deadline.
- There are two signers: your account pays the fee, and the policy key authorizes the mint.
- `completeAndWait` stops waiting after its timeout and then reports the status `TIMEOUT`, even though the transaction may still land. That's why the complete code below checks for `TxStatus.CONFIRMED`.

## Step 4: Find your NFT

A token's unit is its policy id followed by its hex-encoded name. Ask the backend which UTxO at your address holds it:

```java
String unit = AssetUtil.getUnit(policy.getPolicyId(), nftAsset);
holding = backend.getUtxoService().getUtxos(minter.baseAddress(), unit, 1, 1).getValue();
```

The complete code retries this for up to a minute, because a backend's UTxO view can lag behind a confirmed transaction.

## Run it

<details>
<summary>MintNft.java</summary>

```java
package tutorial;

import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.account.Account;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.api.model.Amount;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.api.util.AssetUtil;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.api.model.Utxo;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.backend.api.BackendService;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.backend.blockfrost.common.Constants;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.backend.blockfrost.service.BFBackendService;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.cip.cip25.NFT;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.cip.cip25.NFTMetadata;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.common.model.Networks;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.crypto.KeyGenUtil;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.crypto.Keys;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.function.helper.SignerProviders;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.quicktx.QuickTxBuilder;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.quicktx.Tx;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.quicktx.TxResult;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.quicktx.TxStatus;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.transaction.spec.Asset;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.transaction.spec.Policy;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.transaction.spec.script.RequireTimeBefore;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.transaction.spec.script.ScriptAll;
import com.bloxbean.cardano.client.transaction.spec.script.ScriptPubkey;

import java.math.BigInteger;
import java.time.Duration;
import java.util.List;

public class MintNft {

    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        BackendService backend = new BFBackendService(
                Constants.BLOCKFROST_PREVIEW_URL, System.getenv("BF_PROJECT_ID"));
        Account minter = Account.createFromMnemonic(Networks.preview(), System.getenv("TUTORIAL_MNEMONIC"));

        mint(backend, minter);
    }

    public static void mint(BackendService backend, Account minter) throws Exception {
        // 1. The policy: this key must sign, and only before the deadline
        long deadline = backend.getBlockService().getLatestBlock().getValue().getSlot() + 3600;
        Keys policyKeys = KeyGenUtil.generateKey();
        ScriptAll policyScript = new ScriptAll()
                .addScript(ScriptPubkey.create(policyKeys.getVkey()))
                .addScript(new RequireTimeBefore(deadline));
        Policy policy = new Policy(policyScript, List.of(policyKeys.getSkey()));

        // 2. The token and its CIP-25 metadata
        Asset nftAsset = new Asset("MyFirstNft", BigInteger.ONE);
        NFT nft = NFT.create()
                .assetName(nftAsset.getName())
                .name("My First NFT")
                .image("ipfs://QmYwAPJzv5CZsnA625s3Xf2nemtYgPpHdWEz79ojWnPbdG")
                .description("Minted with Cardano Client Lib");
        NFTMetadata metadata = NFTMetadata.create().addNFT(policy.getPolicyId(), nft);

        // 3. The transaction
        Tx tx = new Tx()
                .mintAssets(policy.getPolicyScript(), nftAsset, minter.baseAddress())
                .attachMetadata(metadata)
                .from(minter.baseAddress());

        TxResult result = new QuickTxBuilder(backend)
                .compose(tx)
                .validTo(deadline)
                .withSigner(SignerProviders.signerFrom(minter))
                .withSigner(SignerProviders.signerFrom(policy))
                .completeAndWait(Duration.ofMinutes(5));

        if (result.getTxStatus() != TxStatus.CONFIRMED)
            throw new IllegalStateException("Not confirmed (" + result.getTxStatus() + "): " + result.getResponse());
        System.out.println("Tx hash   : " + result.getTxHash());

        // 4. Find the token in the minter's wallet
        String unit = AssetUtil.getUnit(policy.getPolicyId(), nftAsset);
        List<Utxo> holding = List.of();
        for (int attempt = 0; attempt < 12 && holding.isEmpty(); attempt++) {
            Thread.sleep(5_000);
            holding = backend.getUtxoService().getUtxos(minter.baseAddress(), unit, 1, 1).getValue();
        }
        if (holding.isEmpty()) throw new IllegalStateException("Token not found yet: " + unit);

        BigInteger quantity = holding.get(0).getAmount().stream()
                .filter(amount -> unit.equals(amount.getUnit()))
                .map(Amount::getQuantity)
                .findFirst().orElseThrow();
        System.out.println("Policy id : " + policy.getPolicyId());
        System.out.println("Quantity  : " + quantity);
    }
}
```

</details>

Running it on Preview prints something like this, with your own values:

```text
Tx hash   : c7050d3519d6d1514c75531e9aa0eb0697d5918882de03d57636245c0b5c1693
Policy id : 787db0464ad195b5c5d0586c3fabfad3d144f6c68e66d1238cf0fef6
Quantity  : 1
```

To see the metadata, look up your transaction hash in a [Preview explorer](https://preview.cardanoscan.io).

## Next steps

- [Multi-sig transfers](/learn/multisig/): the next step in this path, with a script that needs several signatures.
- [CIP-68](/standards/cip68/): NFTs whose metadata can be updated.
- [cardano-client-examples](https://github.com/bloxbean/cardano-client-examples) has more minting samples, such as [minting with QuickTx](https://github.com/bloxbean/cardano-client-examples/blob/main/src/test/java/com/bloxbean/cardano/client/example/quicktx/Minting.java) and [minting with several scripts](https://github.com/bloxbean/cardano-client-examples/blob/main/src/test/java/com/bloxbean/cardano/client/example/quicktx/MultiScriptMinting.java). They aren't updated with every release.
